CROP_DISEASE: Inspect the affected leaves and stems carefully. Remove severely infected parts and apply a recommended fungicide or bactericide. Contact your local agri-extension office for the exact chemical and dosage suitable for your crop and region.
FERTILIZER_SUGGESTION: Apply fertilizer as per soil test results. For most crops, a balanced NPK dose helps. Consider urea for nitrogen, superphosphate for phosphorus, and potash for potassium. Always follow recommended dosage to avoid over-fertilization.
IRRIGATION_GUIDE: Irrigate based on crop growth stage and soil moisture level. Use drip or sprinkler irrigation where possible to save water. Avoid overwatering as it can cause root rot and nutrient leaching.
WEATHER_QUERY: To get accurate weather forecasts, allow location access in the app. You can also check local IMD (India Meteorological Department) forecasts for your district. Plan your farming activities around the weather predictions.
SOIL_HEALTH: Add organic compost, green manure, and vermicompost to improve soil health. Get a soil test done at your nearest agricultural laboratory. Correct pH with lime if soil is acidic, or with gypsum if too alkaline.
STORAGE_GUIDE: Store produce in a cool, dry, and well-ventilated place. Use neem leaves or diatomaceous earth to reduce storage pests. Ensure grain moisture content is below 12-14% before storage. Use airtight containers for seeds.
SEED_GUIDE: Use certified seeds from authorized local suppliers. Choose varieties recommended for your district and season by the local agricultural university. Treat seeds with fungicide before sowing for better germination and disease resistance.
CROP_GROWTH_GUIDE: Follow proper crop cultivation practices: prepare the soil with adequate ploughing and leveling, sow at recommended spacing and depth, provide timely irrigation and nutrients, and monitor for pests and diseases regularly throughout the growth cycle.
PEST_CONTROL: Identify the pest first before applying any pesticide. Use Integrated Pest Management (IPM) practices — combine biological, cultural, and chemical methods. Spray pesticides during early morning or late evening. Always wear protective gear while spraying.
PLANTING_SEASON: The ideal planting season depends on your crop and region. Kharif crops (rice, maize, cotton) are sown in June-July with monsoon rains. Rabi crops (wheat, mustard, gram) are sown in October-November. Summer crops are planted in March-April.
HARVEST_GUIDE: Harvest your crop when it reaches physiological maturity — look for signs like color change, grain hardness, and moisture content. Harvest during dry weather to reduce post-harvest losses. Use proper cutting and threshing techniques for your crop.
ORGANIC_FARMING: Organic farming avoids synthetic chemicals and relies on natural inputs like compost, vermicompost, bio-fertilizers, and bio-pesticides. It improves soil health, reduces pollution, and can fetch premium market prices. Start by replacing chemical fertilizers with organic alternatives gradually.
CROP_SELECTION: Choose crops based on your soil type, water availability, climate, and market demand. Sandy soils suit groundnut and watermelon; clay soils suit rice and wheat. Consider crop rotation to maintain soil fertility. Check with your local agriculture department for recommended crops.
MARKET_GUIDE: Check your nearest APMC mandi for current crop prices. Register on e-NAM (National Agriculture Market) for better price discovery. Consider direct selling to consumers, food processing units, or through Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) for better rates.
GENERAL_AGRICULTURE: Agriculture is the backbone of rural economy. Follow good agricultural practices (GAP) for better yields: proper soil preparation, quality seeds, balanced nutrition, timely irrigation, pest management, and proper post-harvest handling.
